headline: Sensex sinks 548 points as oil price spike and foreign fund outflows drag market below 22,400

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Stock markets tumbled due to a spike in crude oil prices and continued foreign fund outflows.
IT, FMCG, and financial sector stocks dragged the key benchmark indices down.
Retail inflation climbed to 5.54% in September as food inflation surged to 7.74%.
RBI raised concerns regarding pressure on the rupee and volatility in the forex market.
whatHappening: Sensex dropped 548 points while Nifty closed below the 22,400 mark.
HCLTech reported a 21.2% year-on-year rise in Q2 net profit to ₹5,132 crore.
Tata Motors PV expanded its partnership with Stellantis for global vehicle development.
The Indian rupee gained 96 paise to settle at 95.75 against the US dollar.
summary:
Indian equities saw a sharp decline on October 12, with the Sensex sinking 548 points amid surging oil prices and foreign fund sell-offs.
In macro news, retail inflation accelerated to 5.54% for September driven by rising food prices.
On the corporate front, HCLTech posted strong Q2 profit growth while Tata Motors PV announced an expanded tie-up with Stellantis.
